title: Bounded Sobolev localization across two bundle charts
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $M$ be a smooth Hausdorff manifold without boundary of dimension $m\geq1$, and let $E\to M$ be a smooth real vector bundle of finite rank $r\geq0$. Fix coordinate charts $\kappa_U:U\to O_U\subset\mathbf R^m$ and $\kappa_V:V\to O_V\subset\mathbf R^m$, smooth frames of $E$ on $U$ and $V$, a compact subset $K\subset U$, a smooth scalar function $\eta$ on $M$ with compact support contained in $V$, and an integer $s\geq0$. For an $L^2(\mathbf R^m,\mathbf R^r)$ function $f$ vanishing almost everywhere outside $\kappa_U(K)$, let $v_f$ be the measurable section having components $f\circ\kappa_U$ in the $U$ frame and zero outside $U$. Let $T f$ be the components of $\eta v_f$ in the $V$ frame, transported by $\kappa_V$ and extended by zero outside $O_V$. Write $W^{s,2}$ for the space of $L^2$ functions whose distributional derivatives through order $s$ belong to $L^2$, with $\|f\|_{W^{s,2}}^2=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq s}\|\partial^\alpha f\|_2^2$, distributional derivatives being defined by duality against compactly supported smooth test functions. There is $C>0$, depending only on the fixed charts, frames, $K$, $\eta$ and $s$, such that $T f\in W^{s,2}$ and $\|T f\|_{W^{s,2}}\leq C\|f\|_{W^{s,2}}$ for every such $f\in W^{s,2}$. The weak derivatives of $T f$ are given by the distributional Leibniz and chain rules for this formula. This map agrees with multiplication and change of frame and coordinates for the associated distributional sections, where distributions transform by duality with the Jacobian factor on test functions.

proof.text: If $r=0$, $K=\varnothing$, or $\eta=0$, the map is zero and $C=1$ works. Otherwise put $K_U=\kappa_U(K)$. Choose finitely many pairs of concentric balls with compact outer closed balls contained in $O_U$ and inner open balls covering $K_U$. Use [lem-sfb-euclidean-smooth-ball-bump] to obtain their functions $\beta_j$, and set $\chi=1-\prod_j(1-\beta_j)$. The cited product rule shows $\chi$ is smooth; it is one on a neighborhood of $K_U$ and has compact support $H\subset O_U$. Thus $\chi f=f$ almost everywhere for every input under consideration. All choices depend only on $K$ and the fixed $U$ chart.

source.place: Agent integer-order argument supporting Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §2, pp.3–4, integer-order description, (2.2), (2.2 prime), and atlas independence before Lemma 2.3; source WANTED locally and read online.

proof.text: Put $D=\kappa_V(U\cap V)$, $D^{\prime}=\kappa_U(U\cap V)$ and $F=\kappa_U\circ\kappa_V^{-1}:D\to D^{\prime}$. These are open coordinate domains and a smooth diffeomorphism by the chart assumptions. Let $B(y)$ be the smooth matrix converting the $U$ frame to the $V$ frame at $\kappa_V^{-1}(y)$, and let $\eta_V=\eta\circ\kappa_V^{-1}$. Set $A(y)=\eta_V(y)\chi(F(y))B(y)$ on $D$. Its support is contained in the compact set $L=\kappa_V(\kappa_U^{-1}(H)\cap\operatorname{supp}\eta)\subset D$: the intersection is compact since its two compact sets are closed in the Hausdorff manifold. Consequently $A$ extends smoothly by zero to all of $\mathbf R^m$, as does every derivative. Define $Rh=A(h\circ F)$ on $D$, zero elsewhere. Since $\chi f=f$ a.e., the component formula in the question is $Tf=Rf$. The empty overlap or empty $L$ gives the zero map.

source.place: Agent integer-order argument supporting Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §2, pp.3–4, integer-order description, (2.2), (2.2 prime), and atlas independence before Lemma 2.3; source WANTED locally and read online.

proof.text: Here is the measure estimate used below. If $a$ is a smooth matrix supported in $L$ and $h\in L^2(\mathbf R^m,\mathbf R^r)$, apply [lem-sfb-euclidean-jacobian-nonnegative-integrability] to $F^{-1}$ on the Borel compact set $F(L)$. It gives $$\|a(h\circ F)\|_2^2\leq M_a^2 J\|h\|_2^2,\qquad M_a=\sup_L\|a\|,\quad J=\max(1,\sup_{F(L)}|\det D(F^{-1})|).$$ Indeed the changed integrand is $|a(F^{-1}x)h(x)|^2|\det D(F^{-1})(x)|$ on $F(L)$, bounded by the displayed multiple of $|h(x)|^2$. These constants are finite by continuity and compactness. Measurability is also justified: $h$ is integrable on compact $F(L)$ by Cauchy–Schwarz; the integrability clause gives strong measurability of $J_F(h\circ F)$ on $L$, hence of $h\circ F$ there, since $J_F>0$. This positivity follows by differentiating $F^{-1}F=\mathrm{id}$. The same nonnegative identity for indicators of Borel null sets shows inverse images of null sets are null; therefore the formula is independent of all a.e. representatives.

proof.text: For smooth $h$, differentiate the expression for $Rh$ componentwise using [lem-sfb-real-smooth-differentiation]. Induction on the derivative order gives $$\partial^\alpha Rh=\sum_{|\beta|\leq|\alpha|}C_{\alpha\beta}(\partial^\beta h)\circ F.$$ Initially $C_{0,0}=A$. When taking $\partial_i$, replace a coefficient $C$ by $\partial_i C$ with the same $\beta$, and add $C\partial_i F_j$ with index $\beta+e_j$ for each $j$. This explicit recursion proves the formula at the next order. Every coefficient is smooth, has support in $L$, and depends only on $A,F,\alpha,\beta$; extend it by zero. There are no boundary terms, since $L$ is compact inside $D$. Let $N$ be the number of multi-indices of order at most $s$, and let $M$ be the maximum of $1$ and the finitely many $M_{C_{\alpha\beta}}$. The measure estimate and $|\sum_{j=1}^N z_j|^2\leq N\sum_j|z_j|^2$ yield $$\sum_{|\alpha|\leq s}\|\partial^\alpha Rh\|_2^2\leq N^2M^2J\sum_{|\beta|\leq s}\|\partial^\beta h\|_2^2.$$ This uses only finite sums after the cited first-order chain and product rules.

proof.text: For a smooth compactly supported $h$, all the functions in the last display and all products with a test function are continuous and compactly supported; their integrability follows from [lem-sfb-continuous-compact-support-integrable], applied componentwise, also to squared norms. Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-integrable-integration-by-parts] to a real component (regarded as complex-valued), a scalar test function, and each coordinate direction. Its three integrability hypotheses hold as just checked. Repeating the equality shows that the classical derivatives in the recursion represent the distributional derivatives, with sign $(-1)^{|\alpha|}$. Thus $Rh\in W^{s,2}$ and the previous estimate is an estimate in precisely the weak-derivative norm of the question.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-euclidean-sobolev-graph-mollification] with $\Omega=O_U$ and compact $K_U$ to obtain $h_n\in C_c^\infty(O_U,\mathbf R^r)$ with $h_n\to f$ in $W^{s,2}$. The measure estimate shows $Rh_n\to Rf$ in $L^2$. For each $\alpha$, it also shows that the finitely many terms in its recursion converge in $L^2$ to $$g_\alpha=\sum_{|\beta|\leq|\alpha|}C_{\alpha\beta}(\partial^\beta f)\circ F,$$ zero outside $D$. The closed-graph clause of that same node applies to $Rh_n$, proved to be in $W^{s,2}$ in the previous step: $g_0=Rf$, so $Rf\in W^{s,2}$ and $\partial^\alpha Rf=g_\alpha$. Taking limits in the finite squared-norm estimate gives $\|Tf\|_{W^{s,2}}\leq NM\sqrt J\|f\|_{W^{s,2}}$. This constant is positive and depends only on the fixed data. The recursion is the weak Leibniz and chain formula. The auxiliary $\chi$ can be suppressed in that formula: it is one near $K_U$, and outside $K_U$ all distributional derivatives of $f$ vanish locally, directly from their action on tests supported in that complement.

proof.text: Finally let $\psi:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf R^r$ be any smooth compactly supported test vector. Componentwise Jacobian change of variables gives $$\langle Rf,\psi\rangle=\int_{D^{\prime}} f(x)^t A(F^{-1}x)^t\psi(F^{-1}x)|\det D(F^{-1})(x)|\,dx.$$ Cite [lem-sfb-euclidean-jacobian-integral] with real integrands embedded in $\mathbf C$; integrability of both sides follows from the preceding $L^2$ bound and Cauchy–Schwarz, or the integrability criterion. The test vector on the right extends by zero smoothly with compact support in $D^{\prime}$, because $A$ has compact support in $D$. This is exactly the dual action of multiplication by the cutoff and change of frame and coordinates, with the absolute inverse Jacobian. The inserted $\chi$ does not change the distribution supported on $K_U$. The same equality with $\partial^\alpha\psi$ identifies its distributional derivatives with those already obtained by the recursion. In the original charts this proves the asserted agreement for the associated distributional sections, including orientation reversing transitions.
